They contain the incidence hypothesis, domination and rigidity, the stratum conclusions, and the support/absolute-continuity conclusions respectively. The frozen proof establishes the absolute continuity directly, without assuming the source's stronger residual density characterization or q<N.

For any fixed choices of support points, all compact support-ball inputs have positive mass for every epsilon>0, even at relative boundary points or atoms. Keeping only the ith term and raising to N gives exactly theta_i^N times the input mass. The compact output sets are nested and intersect at the image F_i(E), by compactness and convergence of all the shrinking coordinates. Continuity from above gives the compact-set bound, also trivial for zero input mass.

The affine homothety has nonzero ratio theta_i and an inverse on the full continuous space. Taking inverse images of compact target sets gives domination on compact sets, which extends to arbitrary Borel sets by inner regularity of the pushforward measure.

Small positive-mass compact inputs around support points give positive output mass in every neighborhood of their weighted average. The same argument at a repeated input base, which the hypothesis permits, gives convexity of each support.

For q>0, S has positive finite intrinsic q-volume. The midpoint domination bounds mu((E+x)/2) below by 2^(-N) mu(E) for every x in S. The jointly Borel indicator is 1_E(2y−x). Integrating first in x gives |S∩(2y−E)|_q, at most |E|_q, since the map on E is reflection and translation in the affine hull and introduces no 2^q factor. Thus the bound is exactly 2^N mu(S)/|S|_q, first on compact subsets of S and then on Borel sets by inner regularity; outside S the density is zero. In q=0 the single atom has a density relative to counting measure.

Domination places F_i(S_zi) in S_z. If the input dimension were smaller, the affine hull of this image would have zero output mass by intrinsic absolute continuity, but positive mass from the dominated pushforward. Equal dimensions then give identical direction spaces since theta_i>0. This includes atomic incidences.

Every integer output from a stratum remains in the same stratum by incidence rigidity. A same-parity pair shares its midpoint's invariants; consequently each occupied class is counted exactly once and there are at most 2^n. For both hull claims, every hull point is a finite combination of placed support points, and at an integer base the support inclusion proved above applies. The reverse inclusion follows from the generators.

overlap.comparison: Its compatibility equivalence also gives exact sampled hull sections once Minkowski inclusions of supports have been proved; lattice completeness then excludes additional integer bases. It does not prove the inclusions from a measure hypothesis, the measure domination, or dimension/tangent rigidity.

Dependence components of a complete lattice base have disjoint parities and additive budgets. The incidence rigidity proved here makes each such component lie in one support-invariant stratum; thus the earlier parity conclusion is consistent with grouping components. That fact supplies no support dimension or tangent criterion, measure domination, or density bound.
Its same-capacity measures in a common affine space have log-concave representatives; it does not give incidence domination or rigidity of affine hull directions for varying supports.

readability: Tangent space means the direction space of the support affine hull. The midpoint step in the density argument uses two inputs with the same base, as allowed. In the Fubini calculation, x lies in the affine hull and 2y−E is a reflected translate in that hull.
